facts.claim: When access to GPT-4 is taken away, students perform worse than those who never had access, with a 17% reduction in grades for GPT Base.
facts.quote: we additionally find that when access is subsequently taken away, students actually perform worse than those who never had access (17% reduction in grades for GPT Base)

facts.claim: Having GPT-4 access while solving problems makes performance improve by 48% for GPT Base and 127% for GPT Tutor.
facts.quote: our results show that having GPT-4 access while solving problems significantly improves performance (48% improvement in grades for GPT Base and 127% for GPT Tutor).

rejected.claim: Using chatbots produced a positive overall effect on language learning performance ( g = 0. 484) compared to nonchatbot conditions.
rejected.quote: Results indicated that using chatbots produced a positive overall effect on language learning performance ( g = 0. 484), compared to nonchatbot conditions.

rejected.claim: AI tools improved student performance scores (SMD = 0. 86, 95% CI [0. 36, 1. 37], p = 0. 0008, I2 = 54%) in computer programming courses.
rejected.quote: improved student performance scores (SMD = 0. 86, 95% CI [0. 36, 1. 37], p = 0. 0008, I2 = 54%)

rejected.claim: AI tools did not provide a statistically significant advantage in learning success or ease of understanding (SMD = 0. 16, 95% CI [−0. 23, 0. 55], p = 0. 41, I2 = 55%).
rejected.quote: However, AI tools did not provide a statistically significant advantage in learning success or ease of understanding (SMD = 0. 16, 95% CI [−0. 23, 0. 55], p = 0. 41, I2 = 55%)

research.angle: While AI tools can significantly boost scores during practice, unfettered access can cause students to use them as a crutch, leading to worse performance once the tools are removed.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that AI can improve immediate performance and proficiency, but without proper guardrails or pedagogical design, it can hinder the actual acquisition of skills.
research.caveat: The effectiveness of AI tools varies significantly depending on factors like tool functionality, course design, and the presence of specific safeguards.
